done_when: Close starts the review at the same time as its tests, so a round takes about as long as the slower of the two; a red test or a P0/P1 finding still stops the round, and both results are reported together. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body:
The shipped guidance and generated proof tell clients that the completed test result reaches the reviewer, although the reviewer receives only a pending notice.
Raise: Not done. The new call at close.py:215-217 passes the command and pending notice. Yet skill.md:642 and :660, both checked-in host guides, and close.py:550 still say close supplies the test result to the review. This evidence is distinct from the ruling that completed results cannot be available at review start: these claims remain in the material delivered to clients and in doctor and upgrade proof lists.
findings.title: Not done: shipped close guidance contradicts concurrent review

findings.body:
A red test result is printed but never saved when Autoreview fails, so the next worker round loses its diagnostic output.
Raise: Functional. If Autoreview fails twice while the test command returns nonzero, review.run raises; this finally block stores the test output only in memory. Execution skips the later _save at close.py:293, while worker.py:346 reads failed-test output from saved state.
findings.title: A failed review loses the concurrent test failure from the next worker brief

why: Close waits for tests to finish before it starts the review
